messages:
dave: heads-up - our nightly backup-copy lambda in staging logged decryption failures when trying to validate copied objects. not a user-facing outage but reproducible.

leah: what error do we see? kms denied or wrong-key?

dave: stacktrace from staging: 
```
S3ObjectCopy: COPY Succeeded but Decrypt failed: KMS: InvalidCiphertextException: ciphertext refers to a different KMS key
```

tom: interesting. copy succeeded but the metadata on the destination has x-amz-server-side-encryption:aws:kms and x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id set to our old CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/old-key. source had envelope pointing to customer-keystore.

alice: how did the copy end up with the old-key id? the lambda uses an upload service role that should be updated to use the new CMK alias.

leah: possible timeline: we rotated CMK last week (rekey pipeline) and created new-key, updated manifests, but forgot to update the copy lambda's runtime env ALIAS. when role lacks kms:GenerateDataKey on new-key the SDK may fall back to using legacy key id or the copy preserves original metadata. need to confirm.

dave: found audit entry from last rotation: 
```
EventName: CreateKey
UserIdentity: key-rotation-service
RequestParameters: {"KeyUsage":"ENCRYPT_DECRYPT"}
```
and a subsequent IAM change that removed GrantTo: upload-service role for the new CMK.

tom: reproduction idea: run the lambda against a test object, swap the env var to new alias, then remove kms:GenerateDataKey for the role and see behavior. can someone do quick test?

alice: i'll run it in staging now.

encops-bot: scheduled job `kms.repro-copy-test` for staging at 2025-05-01T02:30:00Z by alice  status: queued.

alice: quick notes from repro: with role granted only old-key permissions the copy keeps destination metadata referencing old-key id even when source was encrypted with new-key. when restore tries to decrypt with new-key it fails since metadata points elsewhere.

leah: that's bad for restore automation - manifests assume dest metadata is authoritative. we should not trust header-only key ids during copy if IAM/rotation in-flight.

tom: mitigation suggestions: 
- change copy lambda to fetch envelope metadata from manifest service and re-encrypt explicitly with configured CMK instead of relying on pass-through headers.
- add pre-copy validation: verify role has kms:Decrypt + kms:GenerateDataKey on target CMK; abort copy if check fails.
- detection: a CloudWatch metric for InvalidCiphertextException count from restore jobs and an alert if rate > threshold.

dave: also add an IAM drift watcher for missed grant assignments post-rotation. we had a manual step that got skipped. can we make policy automation enforce grants?

leah: yes - add a rotation checklist automation that asserts upload-service has grants for new-key before cutover. also add a soft rollback toggle for in-progress copies.

alice: action owners:
- tom: update copy lambda to explicit re-encrypt path + pre-copy IAM check (ETA EOD).
- dave: add CloudWatch alarm + restore metric instrumentation (ETA 4h).
- leah: extend rotation pipeline to auto-assign grants and run post-rotation iam-sanity checks (ETA tomorrow).

encops-bot: incident ticket AUTO-12345 created by encops-bot: "staging: backup-copy KMS key-id mismatch causing decrypt failures". priority: P3.

tom: small doc update: add note in restore playbook to consult manifest key id if decryption fails and to attempt decrypt with alternative keys from rotation history (with approval).

leah: will add that. also planning a short drill next week to exercise rotation -> grant propagation -> restore.

alice: good catch everyone. no prod impact yet but this would have failed restores if it slipped post-rotation.

encops-bot: scheduled drill `key-rotation-propagation-drill` for 2025-05-07T15:00:00Z by leah  status: planned.
